assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, turned atomic spectroscopy into a fractional-uncertainty regime near 1e-18. The result is a precision instrument for tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift over millimetre scales and a future redefinition of the second. It is the kind of atomic-physics result in which exquisite theory-experiment agreement is the whole point.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice trapping scheme and demonstrated early strontium clocks. Ye's group pushed the stability and accuracy records and the many-body clock work. A two-person prize is clean. Hall and Hansch's 2005 recognition covered combs, so the lattice-clock step is distinct.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is abundant across Tokyo, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others, and the interpretation is stable. Timing is good because the clocks are already driving redefinition discussions.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views clocks as sufficiently distinct from the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes.
Ion-clock and Sr-clock contributions by other groups (for example Ludlow, Hinkley) are not in the credited names, and I have not independently verified the full priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Loading ultracold atoms into optical lattices to realise the Hubbard model gave a clean, tunable window on many-body quantum physics, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics and single-site imaging. It tells us how a quantum many-body system behaves in a setting where every parameter is controlled, which is fundamental understanding.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and collaborators) provided the proposal; Greiner and Bloch realised the Mott transition in the 2002 experiments, and Bloch's group developed the quantum gas microscope era. Esslinger (fermions) and Cirac are also strong, so a three-name cut forces a hard allocation; Greiner's role in microscopes and the Mott experiment weighs for inclusion.
assessment.maturity: Many laboratories have reproduced and extended these results over more than two decades. The field is mature, though the 2001 BEC and later cold-atom prizes make a further cold-atom prize one the committee must justify as new.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller and Cirac is unresolved and an exclusion would be painful.
Overlap with Bose-Einstein condensation (2001) and laser cooling (1997) prizes.
I rely on memory for exact priority between the Munich and Harvard groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision picture (three-step model) and the strong-field quantum theory explain why harmonics form a plateau and underlie attosecond pulses and orbital imaging. It is conceptually simple, usable as a simple image, and it turned an unexpected observation into predictive understanding.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's semiclassical model (1993) and the Lewenstein et al. quantum theory (1994) are the decisive contributions; the pairing is compact and natural. Others, such as Kulander and Schafer, made parallel simulation contributions and may be named in discussion, so the line of credit is not wholly clear.
assessment.maturity: The model has been tested across hundreds of experiments and is textbook material. Timing is a concern: the 2023 prize went to experimental attosecond pioneers, and the committee may regard this field as recently recognised.
uncertainties: The 2023 prize partially overlaps, and I have a personal collaboration with the Lund group, so I flag a possible conflict of perspective.
Priority claims by Kulander, Schafer and others are not resolved from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed vacuum beats the standard quantum limit of interferometry and is now used in gravitational-wave detectors. It joins deep quantum optics (noise below the vacuum level) with a major working instrument, so the result is fundamental and later useful.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed squeezed-light interferometry in 1981, Kimble's group made early demonstrations of squeezing, and Schnabel's group developed the audio-band and GEO600 implementations. Slusher, Walls, Yuen and Mavalvala, among others, have strong claims that a three-person cut could not cover.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is in routine use at LIGO and Virgo, so confirmation is robust. Recognition would be timely if tied to the observatory impact, but the credit story is crowded.
uncertainties: Early experimental priority between Bell Labs (Slusher) and Kimble is from memory and not verified.
Four credited names plus omitted pioneers make a fair allocation difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(F) opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors and gave a new, unexpected platform for studying unconventional pairing. It was a genuine surprise found by materials exploration rather than by design.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono's 2008 JACS paper is the clear origin, and the two-person configuration is clean. Later raising of Tc to 55 K by Chinese groups (for example Ren, Chen) is not credited and could draw dispute.
assessment.maturity: The discovery was rapidly reproduced worldwide. The mechanism of pairing is still debated, which is a maturity concern even though the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on how this ranks against the cuprate and other superconductivity recognitions.
Credit for subsequent critical-temperature advances is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting flat bands at the magic angle and then observing correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created a new field of tunable correlated matter. The theory-then-experiment story is cleanly aligned with my taste for precise predictive understanding.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's 2018 experiments provided the observation. Cao and others are central to the experimental result but are not in the credited names, so the experimental credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The result has been reproduced by many groups, but only about eight years have passed and the nature of the superconductivity remains unsettled, so this may be premature.
uncertainties: Experimental credit for the first author and others is not captured by the credited names.
The pairing mechanism is unresolved, and I defer to condensed-matter members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling into superconducting circuits and underlies much of modern quantum information hardware. It is a clear, widely used framework with deep physical content, including dispersive readout and ultra-strong coupling.
assessment.attribution: Blais and Wallraff with Schoelkopf published the 2004 theory and experiment that defined the architecture; the three-name set is coherent. Yale colleagues such as Devoret and Girvin made related contributions that could be argued.
assessment.maturity: It is mature and independently confirmed, but the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits reduces the likelihood of a closely related prize so soon.
uncertainties: Recency of the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may argue for waiting.
Overlap in credit with Devoret and Girvin is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade in tweezer arrays produced programmable, strongly interacting quantum systems used for simulation and gates. The physics is genuinely new in how interactions are engineered, though much of the motivation is technological.
assessment.attribution: Lukin and Saffman proposed the blockade-based gates, and Browaeys and Lukin's groups made the decisive array experiments; Saffman's and others' roles overlap with Jaksch et al. who are not credited. A three-person set is workable but contestable.
assessment.maturity: The experiments are replicated by several groups, but the field is still evolving quickly and the application target of a quantum computer is not yet demonstrated, so it is somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Credit of the 2000 Jaksch-Cirac-Zoller blockade proposal is missing from the supplied names.
Whether the physics will stand as distinct from the broader quantum-simulation prize area is unclear.
